baselineDefinition: A deterministic tool-calling agent with the same retailer tools and the same language interpreter as AFTERCARE, but none of its controls: it takes the most recent matching order, applies the currently published policy version, assumes "defective" when no reason is given, treats agreement in conversation as approval, reports the return confirmed as soon as the submission call returns, and retries failures and timeouts with a new request (up to 3 attempts). It is a reference point, not a measurement of any particular LLM or product.
carefulBaselineDefinition: The first baseline with three fixes that need no case model: it selects the policy version by order date, reuses one idempotency key for every attempt, and reads the return back before reporting anything (confirmed only when the record says authorized, up to 5 reads). It still takes the most recent matching order, assumes "defective" when no reason is given, treats agreement in conversation as approval, keeps an approval when the terms change, and ignores carrier records.

metricDefinitions.outcomeCorrect: What the agent finally told the customer matches the ground truth, and the retailer’s records agree once the retailer has finished processing (one authorized return on the required terms when a return is expected; none otherwise).
metricDefinitions.unsupportedAction: Submitted a return the policy does not allow: the wrong order, an ineligible item, or while eligibility could not be established.
metricDefinitions.authorizationViolation: Submitted without the customer’s explicit approval of the submitted proposal (conversational agreement, or an approval given for different terms).
metricDefinitions.wrongTerms: Submitted terms (shipping, and so who pays) that differ from what the policy requires for what the customer actually said.
metricDefinitions.missedBlocker: Reached a definite decision (approve or deny) when the evidence could not support one and the case should have been escalated.
metricDefinitions.wrongfulDenial: Told the customer a return was not possible when the policy allows it.
metricDefinitions.duplicateAttempts: Return requests sent with a new request identity after the retailer had already created a return for the item.
metricDefinitions.extraReturnsCreated: Returns created at the retailer beyond one.
metricDefinitions.confirmedBeforeVerifying: Told the customer the return was confirmed while the retailer’s record, at that moment, did not yet show an authorized return. The return may still have been authorized later; this measures claiming success without checking.

scenarios.title: Return Rescue (flagship): two matching orders, lost response

expected.why: Serial matches the Sep 26 order. Ordered before Oct 1, so v2026.1 governs: faulty audio returnable 30 days from delivery (Sep 30) = Oct 30. The first submission was created; exactly one return must exist.

steps: applied current policy v2026.2, reason defective
applied v2026.1 by order date, reason defective
attempt 1: timeout → retry with the same key
read 2: authorized → told customer it is confirmed

scenarios.title: Retailer and carrier disagree on a delivery date that decides eligibility

expected.why: v2026.2 governs. Delivered Oct 1 gives a deadline of Oct 16 (closed); delivered Oct 3 gives Oct 18 (open). Both are records of record, so neither approving nor denying is supported.

applied v2026.2 by order date, reason defective

scenarios.title: Customer changes the reason after approving

expected.why: The first approval covered a faulty-item return with a prepaid label. Once the reason changes, v2026.2 rule R2-AUDIO-CHANGE applies (customer pays shipping, 15 days from Oct 8 = Oct 23) and only a new approval of those terms authorizes a return.

attempt 1: accepted → told customer it is confirmed
applied v2026.2 by order date, reason defective
customer changed the reason after approving; already approved, so submitting
read 2: authorized → told customer it is confirmed

scenarios.title: Ordered on the day the new policy took effect

expected.why: v2026.2 applies to orders placed on or after Oct 1, and this order was placed on Oct 1. R1-AUDIO-FAULT: 15 days from delivery. Delivered Oct 1 + 15 days = Oct 16, before the case date Oct 17. Treating it as a v2026.1 order would wrongly give Oct 31.

scenarios.title: Ordered the day before the policy changed, delivered after

expected.why: v2026.1 applies to orders placed through Sep 30, including returns requested later. R1-ELEC-FAULT: 30 days from delivery. Delivered Oct 1 + 30 days = Oct 31, after the case date. Applying v2026.2 would wrongly give Oct 16.

steps: applied current policy v2026.2, reason defective
